Physically impossible ring stereo

A drawing can show ring stereo that no real molecule can have: a hydrogen pointing into a small cage, or a small ring fused trans. InChI encodes such a drawing anyway and gives it its own identifier.

$drawn_pic
Proposal, to be discussed. Nothing on this page is implemented yet. Every InChI shown is what standard InChI gives today. Discussion and details: IUPAC-InChI/InChI #287.

A hydrogen pointing into the cage

9-(Methylsulfonyl)-3-oxa-9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonan-7-amine. In a small bicycle like this both bridgehead hydrogens point outwards. The drawing on the left has both bridgehead wedges the same way, so one hydrogen would point into the cage. That molecule cannot exist; the chemist meant the one on the right.

$drawn_pic

As drawn: one H inside

$drawn_tail

A chiral InChI (/m0) for a drawing of an impossible molecule. InChI warns, but the warning does not say what is wrong:

$drawn_warn

$flipped_pic

One wedge flipped: both H outside

$flipped_tail

The real compound: achiral, and the amine carbon becomes a stereocentre (endo/exo). The two drawings of one compound get two different InChIs.

The check: in or out

Look along the line through the two bridgeheads. From one end the three bridges run clockwise, from the other end anticlockwise. So when both bridgehead substituents point out, the two bridgeheads have mirror-image local configurations. Equal configurations mean one points in.

"In" exists only in large cages, around bicyclo[4.4.4] (about 12 bridge atoms). The proposal flags it up to 8 bridge atoms: bicyclo[2.2.1], [2.2.2], [3.2.1], [3.3.1] and similar. The limits are literature values and need checking.

Small rings fused trans

A ring fusion is the same test with a zero-atom bridge. A cyclopropane fused to a cyclohexane must be cis; trans would need a ring of at least 7.

$cis_pic

cis-Bicyclo[4.1.0]heptane

$cis_tail

The real compound (norcarane).

$trans_pic

trans-Bicyclo[4.1.0]heptane

$trans_tail

Cannot exist, yet gets its own InChI, without any warning.

Smaller ringTrans-fused partner
3impossible below 7 (trans-bicyclo[5.1.0] is isolable)
4impossible below 5 (trans-bicyclo[3.2.0] is strained but known)
5 or moreallowed

Small rings and multiple bonds

Related limits, mostly warnings rather than stereo:

FeatureSmallest isolable ringIn InChI
E (trans) double bond8already handled: ring E/Z is ignored below 8
allene9to add to allene support
triple bond8not stereo; warning only
bridgehead double bond (Bredt's rule)about 7 bridge atomsnot stereo; warning only

Also considered: atropisomer axes tied back by a short tether that cannot hold the drawn twist (lower priority), and cages with several bridgehead pairs (the same test per pair; anything harder is left to 3D validators).

What would change

InChI would warn, e.g. "Impossible ring stereo", and name the atoms. The InChI itself stays as it is: InChI identifies what was drawn, not what was meant. Fixing the drawing is up to the person or program that made it.

Your view counts: is a warning enough, are the size limits right, which cases are missing? Use the Comment buttons on this page or the general discussion below.

How to use it

Nothing to switch on yet. Today InChI answers the impossible drawing with a general warning only:

$use_cli

With the proposal, the log would also say what is wrong and name the bridgehead atoms; the InChI would stay the same.

Every InChI on this page is computed by InChI with standard options, not typed in. Proposal: IUPAC-InChI/InChI #287. All features: InChI Specifications.
